title: Kind record (kind_…)
description: One sort of infrastructure thing (decision 14): a NAMED record type whose fields are the kind's attributes, each typed. The name gives the kind nominal identity (two kinds with the same attributes but different names are different kinds — one concept, one symbol); the attributes are an ordinary type-expression `record`, so a dish's `provides` is a value of that type and a need's constraints are a predicate over its fields, evaluated by `check-refinement`. Enumerated attributes are sum types with nullary variants. Extending a kind is publishing a new kind that `supersedes` the old; the old one keeps resolving. Unsigned; `hash` = BLAKE3 over the JCS form with `hash` removed.

name.description: The kind's name, e.g. `relational-database`. Nominal identity together with the attributes.

attributes.description: A type-expression of kind `record` whose fields are the attributes. Field names are snake_case per spec/type-expression.schema.json (`encryption_at_rest`).

attribute_docs.description: One plain-words line per attribute: what it means and its unit. Testimony for a reader, never read by coverage.
